extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys (practitioners involved in claiming benefit or priority)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards for determining whether a later-filed U.S. patent application is entitled to the filing date (benefit) of an earlier-filed U.S. or foreign application, including requirements for written description, enablement, new matter, timing, and procedural filings for priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirement for benefit claims (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to the benefit of the filing date of an earlier-filed application, the later-filed application must be an application for a patent for an invention which is also disclosed in the prior application; the disclosure in the prior application and in the later-filed application must be sufficient to comply with the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112(a) except for the best mode requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclosure of the prior-filed application must provide adequate support and enablement for the claimed subject matter of the later-filed application in compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (written description and enablement). Case law cited: Transco Products, Inc. v. Performance Contracting, Inc., and others. Use form paragraphs 2.09 and 2.10/2.11.01 or 2.38–2.40 where claims are not adequately disclosed or enabled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application benefit (35 U.S.C. 119(e)) — written description and enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), the written description and drawing(s) (if any) of the provisional application must adequately support and enable the subject matter claimed in the nonprovisional application that claims the benefit of the provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisional must 'contain a written description of the invention and the manner and process of making and using it, in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms,' to enable an ordinarily skilled artisan to practice the invention (New Railhead Mfg. v. Vermeer Mfg. Co.). A claim is not required in a provisional, but the provisional's specification/drawings must adequately support later claims; if not, the later nonprovisional is not entitled to the provisional filing date (example: New Railhead facts and holding). Ensure provisional provides (1) written description of subject matter of the claims and (2) enabling disclosure permitting one of ordinary skill to make and use the claimed invention without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim support from provisional — no claim requirement but sufficiency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Although a provisional application need not contain claims, for a later nonprovisional claim to obtain the provisional filing date, the provisional's written description and drawings must adequately support and enable the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim in the nonprovisional is not adequately supported by the provisional, the nonprovisional is not entitled to the provisional's filing date; if that earlier filing date is necessary to overcome a reference or for interference, ensure provisional disclosure adequately provides both written description and enablement for the claim(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation/divisional disclosure must match prior-filed application (no new matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation application must have the same disclosure as the prior-filed application; it must not include anything that would constitute new matter if inserted in the original application. A divisional must be the same as the prior-filed application or include at least the portion of the prior disclosure germane to the divisional claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat continuation/divisional filings as adding new matter. If matter not disclosed in the prior nonprovisional is present, relationship may need to be changed to continuation-in-part. See MPEP §§201.06–201.08. Use form paragraph 2.10.01 when continuation or divisional contains new matter relative to the prior-filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation-in-part entitlement — partial benefit for disclosed subject matter only
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation-in-part (CIP) may include matter not disclosed in the prior-filed application, but only those claims in the CIP that are directed solely to subject matter adequately disclosed in the parent nonprovisional are entitled to the benefit of the parent's filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims reciting features first introduced in the CIP obtain only the CIP's filing date. If the prior application is fatally defective for insufficient disclosure to support allowable claims, a CIP cannot obtain the parent's benefit for newly supplied matter. Case citations: In re Chu; Transco Products v. Performance Contracting; In re Van Lagenhoven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous chain requirement for earliest benefit under 35 U.S.C. 112(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a continuous chain of copending nonprovisional applications, each copending application must disclose the claimed invention of the later-filed application in the manner provided by 35 U.S.C. 112(a) for the later-filed application to be entitled to the earliest filing date in the chain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every link in the chain must satisfy written description and enablement requirements (except best mode). Recent case: Regents of the University of Minnesota v. Gilead Scis., Inc. (2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of prior applications not sufficient for benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim in a subsequently filed application that relies on a combination of prior applications may not be entitled to the benefit of an earlier filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120, because 35 U.S.C. 120 requires that the earlier filed application contain a disclosure which complies with 35 U.S.C.112(a) for each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each earlier application relied upon must itself disclose the claimed invention in the manner required by 112(a); you cannot aggregate disparate disclosures across earlier applications to satisfy 112(a) for a claim under 35 U.S.C. 120. Case cited: Studiengesellschaft Kohle m.b.H. v. Shell Oil Co.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement to 'use' the invention required for benefit (In re Hafner)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim in the later-filed application is not entitled to the benefit of the earlier filing date if the disclosure of the prior-filed application does not enable one skilled in the art to 'use' the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The previously filed application must satisfy all requirements of the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C.112, including sufficient description to enable one skilled in the art to use the invention (In re Hafner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences when prior application is fatally defective
rubrics_metrics.description: If the prior application is found fatally defective for insufficient disclosure to support allowable claims, a later-filed CIP to supply the deficiency is not entitled to the benefit of the first application's filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only claims in the CIP directed solely to subject matter adequately disclosed in the parent get the parent's filing date; claims to newly introduced features get only the CIP filing date. Historical cases: Hunt Co. v. Mallinckrodt Chemical Works and others. Use appropriate rejections under 35 U.S.C.102 where claims entitled only to later dates read on prior art/public disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for examiner communications (2.09, 2.10, 2.10.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a later-filed application's claim for benefit is acknowledged but applicant has not complied with one or more conditions for receiving the benefit under the relevant statutes, the examiner should use heading form paragraph 2.09 and follow with one or more of form paragraphs 2.10–2.11.01 or 2.38–2.40 depending on circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 2.10: 'Disclosure of Prior-Filed Application Does Not Provide Support for Claimed Subject Matter' — insert prior-application number and explain lack of support/enablement, and list specific claims not entitled to benefit if only some claims are affected. Form paragraph 2.10.01: use when continuation/divisional contains new matter and applicant must delete benefit claim or change relationship to continuation-in-part; include examples of matter not disclosed. Examiner notes provide bracket insertion instructions and contextual use guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reference date for patents/application publications when claiming benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine when an issued patent, patent application publication under 35 U.S.C.122(b), or application deemed published under 35 U.S.C.122(b) is available as a reference under 35 U.S.C.102(a)(2) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C.102(e) as of a prior provisional or nonprovisional application's filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§2154.01(b) and 2136.03 for discussion; the critical date analysis affects whether earlier publications/patents are prior art with respect to benefit dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority of foreign application — basic eligibility (35 U.S.C.119(a) etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under certain conditions, a U.S. application may be entitled to the benefit of the filing date of a prior foreign application; the foreign application must be filed in a foreign country which affords similar privileges or in a WTO member country, and the conditions of 35 U.S.C.119(a)-(d) and (f), 172, 365, 386, and 37 CFR 1.55 must be satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foreign application must be for the same invention and the U.S. application must be filed within the statutory time limits (generally 12 months, 6 months for designs) with possible limited extensions. The Director may require certified copies, translations, and other information; failure to timely claim priority may be treated as waiver unless acceptance of an unintentionally delayed claim is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing a subsequent U.S. application claiming foreign priority (37 CFR 1.55(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional U.S. application must be filed not later than twelve months after the foreign application's filing date (six months for design applications), subject to limited restoration procedures; alternatively, entitlement may derive via benefit under 35 U.S.C.120/121 from a subsequent U.S. application filed within that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delayed filing within two months after the 12-month period may be restored under PCT Rule 26bis.3 or by petition if the delay was unintentional; petitions must include priority claim in ADS, petition fee, and a statement that the delay was unintentional. See paragraph (c) for petition contents and filing location rules (applications on/after May 13, 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim content and timing (37 CFR 1.55(d),(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The priority claim must be filed within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the U.S. application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application (for applications under 35 U.S.C.111(a)), and must be presented in an application data sheet (§1.76(b)(6)) identifying the foreign application by number, authority/country, and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications entering U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C.371, adhere to PCT timing. A delayed priority claim can be accepted if accompanied by required petition materials (certified copy, fee, statement of unintentional delay) as described in paragraph (e). If priority claim is filed after the issue fee is paid, patent will not include the priority claim unless corrected by certificate of correction (35 U.S.C.255 and §1.323).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy and translation requirements for foreign priority (37 CFR 1.55(f),(g),(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may require a certified copy of the original foreign application (and translation if not in English). Certified copies must be filed within specified timeframes (generally within the later of four months from actual U.S. filing or sixteen months from foreign filing for 111(a) applications) or a petition with showing of good and sufficient cause is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: certified copy requirement satisfied if a prior-filed U.S. nonprovisional (for which benefit is claimed) contains the certified copy and is identified; participating intellectual property offices under priority document exchange agreements may permit the Office to obtain the copy directly (paragraph (i)). If translation is required, it must be filed with a statement of accuracy. Interim copies clearly labeled and accompanied by cover sheet may be filed under paragraph (j) with later certified copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays, petitions, and standards for accepting late priority claims (37 CFR 1.55(c),(e),(f)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subsequent U.S. application is filed after the normal period but within two months of its expiration, the right of priority may be restored upon petition (PCT Rule 26bis.3) or under this section if delay was unintentional; petitions to accept delayed priority claims must include the priority claim in an ADS, the petition fee, certified copy where required, and a statement that the delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition to restore priority filed on/after May 13, 2015 must be filed in the subsequent application or earliest nonprovisional claiming benefit. For failure to file certified copy timely, a petition showing good and sufficient cause and fee is required. The Director may require additional information when question exists about unintentionality or sufficiency of cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document exchange and interim copy procedures (37 CFR 1.55(i),(j),(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified copy requirement may be satisfied by Office-obtained copies under bilateral/multilateral priority document exchange agreements, or by identifying a prior U.S. nonprovisional that contains a certified copy. Alternatively, an 'Interim Copy' labeled as such plus a cover sheet may be filed within specified time limits, provided a certified copy is later filed within the required period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For priority document exchange: applicant must present priority claim in ADS and provide info necessary for participating foreign office to provide the Office with access. Interim copy requirements: include identification details and file the certified copy later as required; if certified copy not timely, petition with showing of good and sufficient cause is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special statements for applications affected by March 16, 2013 effective date (kin to AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonprovisional application filed on or after March 16, 2013 claims priority to a foreign application filed prior to that date and also contains (or ever contained) a claim to an invention with an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013, the applicant must provide a statement to that effect within specified time limits (generally within the later of four months from actual filing, four months from national stage entry, sixteen months from prior foreign filing, or upon presentation of a first claim with such effective date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is not required to provide the statement if they reasonably believe based on available information that the nonprovisional does not and did not at any time contain such a claim. This helps determine whether certain priority/effective-date rules apply to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-extendable time periods subject to limited statutory/regulatory overrides
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods set forth for priority claims, certified copies, and related procedures are not extendable except as provided by specific statutes or rules (e.g., 35 U.S.C.21(b), PCT Rule 80.5, Hague Agreement Rule 4(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must adhere to the time limits unless a statutory/regulatory provision explicitly allows extension or a petition under specified provisions is granted.
